subject.title: Add an "Approve and Run" action for assistant-suggested terminal commands in the Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw add a Control UI command-proposal path from assistant output to approved local execution, and what structured contract must bind command text, cwd, host, session, risk, reviewer authority, and output routing?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested UX is still missing, but the permanent behavior creates a new command-execution boundary that automation cannot safely define without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design Structured Proposal Contract
options.body: Add a first-class assistant command proposal event/model that reuses exec approval resolution, exact-context binding, risk metadata, and output routing before rendering Approve and Run.

options.title: Keep Markdown Copy-Only
options.body: Leave assistant-authored shell snippets as copy-only markdown and rely on existing exec approvals only after the runtime creates a structured approval request.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Approval Work
options.body: Track this under a larger approvals/tool-confirmation design and avoid a standalone command-card execution path for now.

recommendation.title: Design Structured Proposal Contract
recommendation.body: Add a first-class assistant command proposal event/model that reuses exec approval resolution, exact-context binding, risk metadata, and output routing before rendering Approve and Run.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, Gateway approval contracts, and Control UI execution UX, and history points to steipete as the strongest owner signal for that boundary.
